concept.name: Sign of weakness
concept.definition: The Wyckoff event (SOW) in which price declines to or slightly below the lower boundary of a trading range on increased spread and volume, showing supply in control. Together with the automatic reaction, initial SOWs mark the change of character that precedes markdown.
concept.intuition: The first selloff with real conviction, proving sellers have taken control.
concept.mechanics: The analyst looks for down-moves whose bars widen in spread with expanding volume, breaking toward or through range support. A major SOW that decisively breaks the ice is often retested by a feeble rally that fails at or near the old support, offering a short entry before markdown resumes.
concept.failure_modes: A single wide-range down bar can be a shakeout or news shock rather than genuine supply; an SOW that is quickly recovered on strength negates the bearish confirmation.
concept.misconceptions: An SOW is not merely 'a big red bar'; its meaning comes from context — appearing after distribution events and being followed by feeble, low-volume rallies (LPSYs).
concept.example: After a UTAD fails, a stock drops from 148 to 134 through its range floor on the heaviest volume in months; a weak bounce to 138 fails, confirming the SOW before markdown.

citations.source: The Wyckoff Method: A Tutorial (StockCharts.com ChartSchool, by Roman Bogomazov and Michael Lipsett)
